verdict.rationale: First-party docs state that self-hosting runs the complete Flagsmith platform on your own infrastructure. They document Docker setups for a full environment and Kubernetes/OpenShift deployment with Helm charts and operators, and they emphasise data sovereignty. A community hands-on evaluation of self-hosted feature-flag tools included Flagsmith, which corroborates that self-hosting works, though that user found it less polished. Missing for 10: evidence of feature parity between self-hosted and cloud (e.g., the managed experimentation warehouse), and explicit licensing or open-source terms for the self-hosted core.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Self-hosting Flagsmith allows you to run the complete Flagsmith platform within your own infrastructure, giving you full control over your data, security policies, and deployment environment.
You can use Docker to set up an entire Flagsmith Feature Flag environment locally
Kubernetes and OpenShift: Full Kubernetes deployment with Helm charts and operators
**Data sovereignty**: Keep your feature flag data within your own infrastructure
